node.content: Baikonur Cosmodrome (in the desert steppe of Kazakhstan) was the Soviet Union's primary launch facility; major early missions such as Sputnik and Vostok 1 launched from there. The Soviet Union kept Baikonur’s location secret for years by providing misleading coordinates.
node.summary: Baikonur Cosmodrome: USSR’s primary launch facility in Kazakhstan; its location was long kept secret using misleading published coordinates.

edge.context: Note says action was in response to Sputnik.

node.content: In response to Sputnik, President Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the National Aeronautics and Space Act on July 29, 1958, creating NASA. The new agency absorbed NACA (the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics) and several U.S. military research programs.
node.summary: Eisenhower signed the National Aeronautics and Space Act (1958), creating NASA in response to Sputnik; NASA absorbed NACA and military research programs.

node.content: Cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961, aboard Vostok 1. The flight lasted 108 minutes and completed one orbit of Earth. Sergei Pavlovich Korolev personally oversaw the mission from the control center at Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
